label: Discrete Mathematics
shortDescription: Logic, sets, proofs, combinatorics, graphs, and number theory — the mathematical foundation of computer science.
modulesDescription: Read the discrete mathematics chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogTitle: Learn Discrete Mathematics for Free | CalcPath

topics.title: Logic and Proofs
topics.description: Propositions and the five connectives; functional completeness of NAND alone; equivalences, contrapositive and vacuous truth; quantifiers and their negation; rules of inference and the classic fallacies; direct proof, contraposition and contradiction with the irrationality of the square root of 2; and induction, strong induction and well-ordering shown to be equivalent.

topics.title: Sets and Functions
topics.description: Set operations and the double-inclusion method used throughout; distributive and De Morgan laws by element chasing; inclusion-exclusion for two and three sets; functions, images and preimages; injectivity and surjectivity characterised by left and right inverses; bijections and composition; power sets with the count 2 to the n; and Cantor's theorem proved by the diagonal set.

topics.title: Relations and Equivalence
topics.description: Binary relations, their matrices and digraphs; the five properties shown independent by explicit witnesses; the correspondence between equivalence relations and partitions proved in both directions; congruence modulo n; transitive closure as a union of powers and as a smallest relation; partial orders, Hasse diagrams and maximal elements; and total orders with topological sorting.

topics.title: Combinatorics
topics.description: The sum and product rules with counterexamples when their hypotheses fail; permutations and combinations derived by uniform overcounting; Pascal's identity proved combinatorially; the binomial theorem with Vandermonde and the hockey-stick identity; stars and bars as a bijection; the pigeonhole principle with its generalised form and classic applications; and inclusion-exclusion with derangements as a corollary.

topics.title: Graph Theory
topics.description: Graphs, degrees and the handshake lemma by double counting; edge bounds forcing connectivity; walks, paths and cycles; four characterisations of a tree proved in a cycle of implications; bipartite graphs characterised by the absence of odd cycles; and Euler's theorem in both directions, with the Konigsberg bridges as a corollary.

topics.title: Number Theory
topics.description: The division algorithm with existence and uniqueness; primes, the square-root test and Euclid's infinitude; the Euclidean algorithm with its logarithmic bound and Fibonacci worst case; Bezout's identity from the extended algorithm; modular arithmetic, inverses and linear congruences; fast exponentiation by squaring; Fermat's little theorem, Euler's totient and the Chinese remainder theorem; and RSA with its correctness proved.
